contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #204: Tensor saturation for even spin groups.

Audit the continuation mechanism for type-D schedules with dominant polygonal shape, integral root pairings, root-lattice endpoint congruence, at-most-one-zero moving label, and the standing rank induction and absence of an integral schedule.

definitions.schedule: Definition def:schedule in 02-real-schedules.tex, including ordered simultaneous switches, nonnegative position gap and total, and endpoint in W xi
definitions.local_link: Conditions (a)-(c) in 03-lattice-continuation.tex:302-313, not merely an augmented root relation
definitions.scope: Exploratory audit of prop:continuation and int:half-kernel; all other manuscript branches remain unverified

contexts.statement: Type-D corank-one schedule continuation in every rank l>=2, for integral-root-pairing labels and a polygonal dominant shape with slopes in the relative interior of its endpoint chamber face. No moment solution, rank induction, or zero-coordinate bound is assumed.

definitions.augmented_state: An exact admissible schedule with l+1 roots generating Q(D_l), coefficient vector a-(1-s)d at some 0<s<1, a integral and d half a primitive nonzero root relation
definitions.rank_drop: A real schedule for the same labels and shape with at most l switches whose position-root span is proper
definitions.formal_scope: Only the universal core declarations in research/continuation/Main.lean are kernel checked; full geometric assembly requires independent mathematical review

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 204 (Tensor saturation for even spin groups.; papers: Tensor saturation for even spin groups; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Manuscript thm:main: for dominant integral weights of Spin(2n), n>=2, whose sum lies in Q(D_n), tensor invariant occurrence is equivalent to occurrence at every positive integral dilation. This is a target assertion, not an accepted assumption.

Manuscript prop:basic-schedule: every dominant-increment shape for a real moment solution has a real schedule with a root basis, limiting local-cover property, and possibly fewer switches after simplification.
Manuscript lem:schedule-moment: a real schedule gives a real moment solution, without a lattice hypothesis, including subsystems and orthogonal central coordinates.

Manuscript lem:block-reduction and lem:hard-case: under rank induction and no integral schedule, every real schedule with at most l switches has exactly l independent roots and two odd unbalanced unicyclic components.

Manuscript int:half-kernel: l+1 roots generating Q(D_l) with a nonintegral half-integral exact base admit either primitive half-relation orientation d with integral m0+d, absolute coefficient and gap derivatives at most one, and d_i=L.gamma_i for a common vector L.
Manuscript prop:continuation: under the standing assumption of no integral schedule, no local link satisfying the exact conditions (a)-(c) can exist.
The continuation proof requires rank-two collision replacements to preserve exact displacement, full lattice generation, primitive half-kernel directions, integral extrapolation, and admissibility.

The continuation proof requires its stated rank-two diamonds and common-potential candidate times to yield a terminating weakly ordered admissible list, including persistent ties and polygonal shape breaks.
The continuation proof requires removal strictness at every interior continuation parameter and compactness plus right extension to attain parameter one.
Manuscript prop:strict-count and prop:knot-count, together with direct and tied local-link constructions, force an integral schedule in the exceptional configuration using prop:continuation.

Manuscript thm:integral-schedule: a real moment solution for integral root-pairing labels with lambda+mu-xi in Q and any dominant-increment shape gives an integral schedule in permutation type or D_l with at most one zero coordinate of mu.
Manuscript prop:columns: an integral schedule for a shape concatenating fundamental columns yields a nonzero intertwiner V(lambda) tensor V(mu) to V(xi).
Manuscript lem:flag-composition: highest-to-highest intertwiners nonzero at flow-ordered flags compose nontrivially on the Cartan summand.
Manuscript prop:zero-tail: tensor occurrence for D_n weights supported on the first r<=n-2 axes yields doubled-weight occurrence in D_(r+1) after appending one zero.

For every rank l>=2, every augmented state as defined admits either an integral schedule or a rank-drop schedule for the same labels and shape. At a fixed nearby parameter, collision sorting uses at most (l(l-1))^(l+1)-1 replacements. This all-rank assertion is a candidate theorem pending independent review.

The declarations in namespace Continuation prove interior integer-hit rigidity, median and tie laws for zeros of sums of arbitrary strictly increasing functions, all eight A2 first-time descent inequalities and lexicographic replacement, finite-state normal forms and cardinal bounds, orthogonal parity singularity, common-potential existence from a one-dimensional kernel and a nonzero fixed vector, and compact right-extension reaching one. These are universal core lemmas, not the entire schedule theorem.

import Mathlib

namespace Continuation

theorem interior_integer_hit
    (s d : ℝ) (z : ℤ) (hs : 0 < s) (hs' : s < 1)
    (hd : |d| ≤ 1) (hz : (1 - s) * d = (z : ℝ)) :
    d = 0 := by
  have hsmall : |(1 - s) * d| < 1 := by
    rw [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (by linarith : 0 < 1 - s)]
    calc
      (1 - s) * |d| ≤ (1 - s) * 1 :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hd (by linarith)
      _ < 1 := by linarith
  rw [hz, abs_lt] at hsmall
  have hzsmall : (-1 : ℤ) < z ∧ z < 1 := by
    exact_mod_cast hsmall
  have hz0 : z = 0 := by omega
  have hmul : (1 - s) * d = 0 := by simpa [hz0] using hz
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hmul).resolve_left (by linarith)

theorem root_sum_time_strict_between
    (f g : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : StrictMono f) (hg : StrictMono g)
    (a b c : ℝ) (ha : f a = 0) (hb : g b = 0)
    (hc : f c + g c = 0) (hab : a < b) :
    a < c ∧ c < b := by
  constructor
  · by_contra hn
    have hca : c ≤ a := le_of_not_gt hn
    have hfc : f c ≤ f a := hf.monotone hca
    have hgc : g c < g b := hg (lt_of_le_of_lt hca hab)
    linarith
  · by_contra hn
    have hbc : b ≤ c := le_of_not_gt hn
    have hgc : g b ≤ g c := hg.monotone hbc
    have hfc : f a < f c := hf (lt_of_lt_of_le hab hbc)
    linarith

theorem root_sum_time_tie
    (f g : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : StrictMono f) (hg : StrictMono g)
    (a c : ℝ) (ha : f a = 0) (hb : g a = 0)
    (hc : f c + g c = 0) :
    c = a := by
  rcases lt_trichotomy c a with h | h | h
  · have hfc := hf h
    have hgc := hg h
    linarith
  · exact h
  · have hfc := hf h
    have hgc := hg h
    linarith

def MedianOrder (i j h : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (i < j ∧ i < h ∧ h < j) ∨
  (i = j ∧ h = i) ∨
  (j < i ∧ j < h ∧ h < i)

theorem root_sum_median_order
    (f g : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : StrictMono f) (hg : StrictMono g)
    (i j h : ℝ) (hi : f i = 0) (hj : g j = 0)
    (hh : f h + g h = 0) :
    MedianOrder i j h := by
  rcases lt_trichotomy i j with hij | hij | hij
  · exact Or.inl ⟨hij, root_sum_time_strict_between f g hf hg i j h hi hj hh hij⟩
  · subst j
    exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨rfl, root_sum_time_tie f g hf hg i h hi hj hh⟩)
  · have hm := root_sum_time_strict_between g f hg hf j i h hj hi
      (by linarith) hij
    exact Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hij, hm⟩)

theorem a2_diamond_descent (i j h : ℝ) (hm : MedianOrder i j h) :
    (j < i → j < i) ∧
    (h < j → i < j) ∧
    (h < i → j < i) ∧
    (i < j → i < j) ∧
    (i < j → h < j) ∧
    (j < h → j < h) ∧
    (j < i → h < i) ∧
    (i < h → i < h) := by
  rcases hm with ⟨_, _, _⟩ | ⟨_, _⟩ | ⟨_, _, _⟩ <;>
    repeat' constructor <;> intro H <;> linarith

theorem pair_replacement_lex
    (prefix suffix : List ℝ) (a b c d : ℝ) (hca : c < a) :
    List.Lex (· < ·) (prefix ++ c :: d :: suffix)
      (prefix ++ a :: b :: suffix) := by
  exact List.Lex.append_left _ (List.Lex.rel hca) prefix

theorem finite_sorting_normal_form
    {A V : Type*} [Fintype A] [LinearOrder V]
    (score : A → V) (step : A → A → Prop)
    (decreases : ∀ {a b}, step a b → score b < score a) (start : A) :
    ∃ finish, Relation.ReflTransGen step start finish ∧
      ∀ next, ¬ step finish next := by
  classical
  let reached : Finset A :=
    Finset.univ.filter (fun a => Relation.ReflTransGen step start a)
  have hne : reached.Nonempty := by
    refine ⟨start, ?_⟩
    simp [reached, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl]
  obtain ⟨finish, hfinish, hmin⟩ := reached.exists_min_image score hne
  have hreach : Relation.ReflTransGen step start finish := by
    simpa [reached] using hfinish
  refine ⟨finish, hreach, ?_⟩
  intro next hstep
  have hnext : next ∈ reached := by
    simpa [reached] using hreach.tail hstep
  exact (not_lt_of_ge (hmin next hnext)) (decreases hstep)

theorem strict_descent_card_bound
    {A V : Type*} [Fintype A] [LinearOrder V]
    (score : A → V) (m : ℕ) (states : Fin (m + 1) → A)
    (h : StrictAnti (fun i => score (states i))) :
    m + 1 ≤ Fintype.card A := by
  have hinj : Function.Injective states := by
    intro i j hij
    exact h.injective (congrArg score hij)
  simpa using Fintype.card_le_of_injective states hinj

theorem orthogonal_parity_singularity
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (P : Matrix I I ℝ) (ho : P * P.transpose = 1)
    (hp : (-1 : ℝ) ^ Fintype.card I * P.det = -1) :
    (1 - P).det = 0 := by
  have hid : (-P) * (1 - P).transpose = 1 - P := by
    rw [Matrix.transpose_sub, Matrix.transpose_one, mul_sub, mul_one, neg_mul, ho]
    abel
  have hdet := congrArg Matrix.det hid
  rw [Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_neg, Matrix.det_transpose, hp] at hdet
  linarith

theorem common_potential_of_fixed_vector
    {E V : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V]
    (B : V →ₗ[ℝ] E) (G : E →ₗ[ℝ] V) (P : E →ₗ[ℝ] E)
    (ht : B.comp G = LinearMap.id - P)
    (hG : Function.Injective G) (d : V)
    (hk : ∀ v, B v = 0 → ∃ a : ℝ, v = a • d)
    (x : E) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hfix : P x = x) :
    ∃ L, G L = d := by
  have hzero : B (G x) = 0 := by
    have heq := LinearMap.congr_fun ht x
    simpa [hfix] using heq
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hk (G x) hzero
  have ha0 : a ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    have hGx : G x = 0 := by simpa [hz] using ha
    apply hx
    apply hG
    simpa using hGx
  refine ⟨a⁻¹ • x, ?_⟩
  rw [map_smul, ha, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ ha0, one_smul]

theorem endpoint_of_compact_right_extension
    (S : Set ℝ) (hcompact : IsCompact S) (hne : S.Nonempty)
    (hbound : ∀ s ∈ S, s ≤ 1)
    (hextend : ∀ s ∈ S, s < 1 → ∃ t ∈ S, s < t) :
    1 ∈ S := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := hcompact.exists_isGreatest hne
  have hsle : s ≤ 1 := hbound s hs.1
  have hseq : s = 1 := by
    by_contra hne
    obtain ⟨t, ht, hst⟩ := hextend s hs.1 (lt_of_le_of_ne hsle hne)
    exact (not_lt_of_ge (hs.2 ht)) hst
  simpa [hseq] using hs.1

end Continuation
